audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.spikes named no Malzahar spike. His real one is Nether Grasp falling from 140s at rank 1 to 80s at rank 3.
audit.why: Riot R cd 140/110/80 — a 60-second swing that decides how often he can remove a member of your team.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page describes Void Shift as 'his passive shield' in breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d and report[5].t. It is not a shield — it grants damage reduction AND crowd-control immunity until he takes damage. That inverts the single most important instruction in the matchup: an uncharged Galio taunt or knockup does nothing to a Malzahar who has not been damaged. Separately, Call of the Void SILENCES; four places on the page call it a snare or a root.
audit.why: Riot passive text: 'Malzahar gains massive damage reduction and crowd control immunity, lingering for a short period after taking damage.' Riot Q text: 'deal Magic Damage and silence enemy champions.' Neither says shield, snare or root.
audit.corrected: tldr, winCon, enemyWin, tradeGood, tradeBad, breakdown.early, dontsFull[1].d and report[5].t now say damage reduction plus CC immunity and instruct chipping him first; spikes[0].text, wants.foe[1] and content mid now say silence.
sources: kit: Malzahar P and Q text
kit: Galio W hardCC, E knockup

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[3].text claims Shield of Durand 'completely negates his ultimate's true damage'. Nether Grasp deals magic damage, not true damage, and 'completely negates' is a magnitude the kit does not give. Content mid also calls Nether Grasp 'a stationary root'; it is a suppression delivered by a channel.
audit.why: Riot R text: 'channels the essence of the Void to suppress an enemy champion over a zone of damaging negative energy' — magic damage, channel, suppress. The kit's channel flag confirms any CC cancels it.
audit.corrected: Both rewritten around the real interaction: the channel ends outright to a taunt or knockup.
sources: kit: Malzahar R text and channel flag

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns had no digit (lint COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT), and dosFull[2].d invented a 'fifteen-second invitation' for an ultimate whose shortest cooldown is 80 seconds.
audit.why: Nether Grasp is 140/110/80 and Call of the Void is a flat 6s at every rank — those are the two numbers that govern every step-up.
audit.corrected: Both rewritten with the real numbers.
sources: kit: Malzahar R cd 140/110/80 range 700, Q cd 6 range 900

audit.whatIsWrong: missingInteractions carries an 'execute-threshold' rule saying Malefic Visions threatens a threshold kill.
audit.why: Riot's E text says the visions PASS ON to a nearby unit if the target dies — there is no health threshold anywhere in it. The 'execute' derived flag is a parse misfire. I wrote no threshold claim.

edits.before: Levels 3-5 you should be walking him down every time his Voidlings shove the wave into you, since his kit has zero disengage and your E lets you close the gap before his snare lands. notes: This matchup carried the worst factual errors of my seven. Void Shift was described as 'his passive shield' in three places — it is damage reduction plus CROWD-CONTROL IMMUNITY, which means an undamaged Malzahar simply ignores a Galio taunt or knockup. That inverts the correct play and is now stated with the chip-first sequencing. Call of the Void was called a snare or root in three places; Riot's text says silence. spikes[3].text claimed Nether Grasp deals true damage (it is magic) and that W 'completely negates' it (a magnitude with no source). The missingInteractions 'execute-threshold' rule for Malefic Visions is WRONG — Riot's text describes the visions passing on when the target dies, not a health threshold — and I wrote nothing from it. One report[] entry edited, on the fabricated-ability-description ground (report[5].t named a passive shield that does not exist). Chart agreed across layers; no side/win edits.
